Card 1 — three tasks, one of them without answers

Regression and classification learn from an answer column, so we can count their mistakes. Clustering has no answer column: it looks for groups that nobody named in advance.

taskwhat comes outanswer column?how we judge it
Regressiona number: minutes per taskyesaverage miss, R² (session 5)
Classificationa known label: bankrupt or notyesrecall, precision, AUC, cost (session 6)
Clusteringgroups nobody namednocan you name the groups, act on them, and get them again?
customer segments topics of complaints shares that move together "branches like this one" anomalies: points in no group a step before optimisation

A real example of the last one: Ozon Tech clusters warehouse cabinets by how full they are (Affinity Propagation, then agglomerative clustering) to narrow the search before placing goods. "Maths in the warehouse: how to optimise chaos", Habr, 2025 (the article is in Russian).

Card 2 — every algorithm has its own idea of a group

Five toy shapes, five algorithms. Each shape is standardized; k-means, Ward and the mixture get the right number of groups, DBSCAN and HDBSCAN find it themselves. Grey dots are noise: points the algorithm put in no group. No column wins every row.

k-means and WardRound groups of similar size. Straight borders, so they cut moons and rings. On a cloud with no groups they still return k.
DBSCAN and HDBSCANA group is a dense area. Any shape, no k, loners become noise. DBSCAN needs a radius and uses one for everything: in row 2 it breaks a crumb off the loose blob. HDBSCAN needs only the smallest group you care about and copes with different densities: the practical default.
Gaussian mixtureStretched ellipses and soft membership: each point gets a probability for every group.

The full picture, 11 algorithms on 6 shapes, and a table of settings, scale and use cases: scikit-learn, Overview of clustering methods. The original figure: Comparing different clustering algorithms on toy datasets.

Card 3 — PCA turns the axes

Weekly returns of Lukoil and Rosneft, January 2023 to September 2026. Two oil companies move together, so the cloud is a stretched oval. PCA rotates the axes: the first runs along the oval, the second across it.

A component is a weighted sumNew axis 1 = 0.71 × Lukoil + 0.71 × Rosneft: "oil companies in general". The weights are called loadings.
Keep the big onesAxis 1 holds 88% of the spread. One number per week instead of two, most of the movement kept.
Thirty sharesPC1 = the market (54% of the spread, 0.95 with the MOEX index), PC2 = oil companies, PC3 = gold against steel. 30 columns become 3.

Card 4 — a map is not evidence

The same 5,000 complaints, each a vector of 384 numbers, squeezed onto a page three ways. Colours are the eight k-means clusters, found in the full 384 dimensions.

PCAStraight axes, readable components. Curved structure gets flattened: here one blob with overlapping clusters.
t-SNE and UMAPKeep each point's nearest neighbours near it. Islands appear; UMAP is faster and keeps a little more of the big picture.
How not to be fooledIsland sizes mean nothing. Gaps between islands may mean nothing. Settings change the picture. The proof is a table, not the map.

How to Use t-SNE Effectively and Understanding UMAP: two interactive explanations worth ten minutes each.

Card 5 — clustering at work: a checklist

Not "pick an algorithm and go". Ten steps, from the question to the report.

  1. Question and action. What will you do differently for each group? No action, no clustering.
  2. The unit. One point is a client, a day, a share, a text?
  3. Turn it into numbers. Numbers: standardize. Texts: TF-IDF or an encoder. Time series: returns, or a profile per period.
  4. Too many columns? Compress: PCA for straight structure, UMAP before clustering texts.
  5. Algorithm by the shape you expect. Round groups: k-means. Odd shapes, noise, unknown number of groups: HDBSCAN (or DBSCAN). Nested groups: hierarchical.
  6. Settings. k: elbow and silhouette, then "can I name them". HDBSCAN: the smallest group worth acting on. DBSCAN: eps at the bend of the sorted k-distance line.
  7. Read the clusters. Centers, typical words, the closest examples.
  8. Check stability. Another seed, another sample: are the groups still there?
  9. Name them, then check. An assistant names at scale; you read the texts.
  10. Report. A table and one picture; the conclusion in words, separately.
